states.name: Kentucky
states.regulator: Kentucky Board of Home Inspectors (Kentucky Real Estate Authority, Public Protection Cabinet)
states.field_training: 16 of the 64 hours are field training (max 8 lab hours), plus 3 unpaid home inspections under direct supervision of a KY-licensed inspector
states.ce: 28 hours per biennial period (14 per license year), incl. 3 hrs KY law and 3 hrs report writing taken in person
states.renewal: Biennial license period per 831 KAR 2:040; renewal fee charged per year of licensure
states.fees: $250 application; $200 per year of licensure on renewal; $250 late renewal
states.notes: Requires state and FBI background checks. The regulations tie CE to odd/even renewal years; confirm the current renewal cycle with the board.

states.name: Louisiana
states.regulator: Louisiana State Board of Home Inspectors
states.field_training: Included in the 130: 90 hrs approved coursework, 30 hrs in-field platform training, and 10 live fee-paid inspections with a certified infield trainer
states.exam: NHIE (board-approved) plus the board's Standards of Practice/Code of Ethics exam and report-writing seminar
states.insurance: E&O min $300,000/yr and general liability min $300,000/yr, each with max $5,000 deductible
states.ce: 20 hours per year (30 hours for first renewal)
states.fees: $200 application; $100 renewal; $5 state fee per inspection, reported monthly
states.notes: Louisiana charges a $5 per-inspection state fee, with a monthly report due even when no inspections are done. Board rules are at LAC 46:XL.

states.name: Maine
states.notes: Maine has no statewide home inspector license; licensing bills (e.g., LD 168 in the 119th Legislature) have been proposed but none is in effect. Normal business registration applies.

states.name: Maryland
states.regulator: Maryland State Commission of Real Estate Appraisers, Appraisal Management Companies and Home Inspectors (Maryland Department of Labor)
states.field_training: 72-hour course must be completed on-site (classroom), not virtually
states.ce: 30 hours per renewal (none for first renewal), incl. 2 hrs report writing and 2 hrs standards of practice
states.notes: Maryland adopted new Standards of Practice; the 2-hour standards-of-practice CE requirement is delayed until 1/1/2027.

states.name: Massachusetts
states.credential: License (Associate Home Inspector, then Home Inspector)
states.regulator: Massachusetts Board of Registration of Home Inspectors (Division of Occupational Licensure)
states.field_training: Associate: 25 inspections under direct supervision (up to 10 may be approved mock inspections). Full license: at least 1 year as associate plus 100 more supervised inspections
states.ce: 12 hours per 2-year cycle (incl. 4 hrs 266 CMR/SOP and 1 hr ethics)
states.renewal: Every 2 years (expires May 31 of even years)
states.fees: Associate $225; Home Inspector initial $338; renewal $225; late renewal $57
states.notes: Two-tier system: start as an Associate under a licensed supervisor, then upgrade after 1 year and 100 inspections. Fee figures come from mass.gov pages that blocked direct fetching.

states.name: Michigan
states.notes: Michigan has no statewide home inspector license; past licensing bills (e.g., 2021 HB 4500) did not pass, and no 2025-2026 licensing bill was found enacted.

states.name: Minnesota
states.notes: No statewide license. Some cities (Minneapolis, St. Paul, Maplewood and others) require a city-licensed Truth-in-Sale of Housing (TISH) evaluator for point-of-sale evaluations.

states.name: Mississippi
states.regulator: Mississippi Real Estate Appraisal Board, Mississippi Home Inspection Division (Home Inspector Regulatory Board)
states.field_training: 60-hour course may include field work as prescribed by the board
states.insurance: General liability min $250,000 and E&O min $250,000 per occurrence
states.fees: $175 application/exam; $325 license (initial and renewal); non-resident reciprocal application $50
states.notes: 2024 HB 1324 revived the Home Inspector Regulatory Board and moved oversight from the Real Estate Commission to the Real Estate Appraisal Board (effective July 1, 2024). Applicants must be 21; an optional New Home designation needs a builder license plus ICC certification.

states.name: Missouri
states.notes: No statewide license. 2026 HB 1832 would have created a Missouri Home Inspectors' Board, but it stalled in committee and did not become law.

states.name: Montana
states.regulator: Montana Department of Labor and Industry, Business Standards Division (Home Inspector Program)
states.insurance: E&O, minimum $125,000; must also keep membership in a national home inspection association
states.ce: None required by the state (national association CE rules may apply)
states.notes: New: HB 225 replaced business registration with an individual license effective Jan 1, 2026; active registrants were converted automatically. Renewal cycle not stated in the sources reviewed.

states.name: Nebraska
states.regulator: Nebraska Secretary of State, Licensing Division
states.notes: Registration only, with no education or exam requirement, in effect since Jan 1, 2023 (LB 423, 2021). Inspectors must register before inspecting and list any national certification held.

states.name: Nevada
states.regulator: Nevada Real Estate Division (Inspectors of Structures)
states.field_training: Observe 25 fee-paid inspections by a certified general/master inspector or approved instructor
states.exam: State-approved Inspector of Structures exam (NHIE-based, via Pearson VUE)
states.insurance: E&O min $100,000 and general liability min $100,000
states.ce: 20 hours per 2-year renewal (incl. 3 hrs safety, 2 hrs NRS/NAC 645D)
states.fees: NRS: $100 application + $250 issuance/renewal + $15 technology fee; Division lists $365 for initial residential certificate; exam $100
states.notes: Nevada certifies residential, general and master inspectors; the general and master tiers need more hours and inspections.

states.name: New Hampshire
states.regulator: New Hampshire Board of Home Inspectors (Office of Professional Licensure and Certification)
states.insurance: Proof of liability insurance required; rules do not set a minimum amount
states.fees: $200 biennial renewal; application fee not confirmed from official page
states.notes: No minimum field-inspection count. Criminal background check required.

states.name: New Jersey
states.regulator: New Jersey Home Inspection Advisory Committee (Division of Consumer Affairs)
states.field_training: At least 40 hours of unpaid field-based inspections under a licensed inspector (part of the 180); alternative path: 250 fee-paid supervised inspections
states.notes: Current fee schedule not confirmed (a 2006 rule listed $125 application and $500 initial license). The associate inspector class was eliminated in 2005.

states.name: New Mexico
states.regulator: New Mexico Regulation and Licensing Department, Home Inspectors Board
states.field_training: 80 hours of field training including at least 30 parallel inspections
states.insurance: E&O min $250,000 aggregate and professional liability min $250,000
states.notes: The 80 classroom hours may be taken online. Other routes exist by experience or by out-of-state credentials. Board rules were updated in April 2024.

states.name: New York
states.regulator: New York Department of State, Division of Licensing Services
states.field_training: 40 of the 140 hours are unpaid field-based inspections under a licensed inspector, PE or architect; alternative: 100 supervised inspections
states.exam: NYS home inspector exam or NHIE
states.notes: Applicants need a high school diploma or equivalent and must have no disqualifying criminal convictions.

states.name: North Carolina
states.regulator: North Carolina Home Inspector Licensure Board (Office of State Fire Marshal)
states.field_training: Included in the 200: at least 120 hrs classroom plus at least 80 hrs field instruction with at least 10 site visits
states.insurance: General liability $250,000 plus one of: E&O $250,000, a surety bond (min $5,000), or $5,000-$10,000 net assets
states.ce: 12 hours per year (16 per year for the first 3 years for some new licensees)
states.fees: $35 application; $80 exam; $160 license issuance/renewal; $30 late renewal
states.notes: Board rules were amended effective June 1, 2026; licensees must file a general liability certificate each January naming the Board as holder. GCs, architects and PEs licensed 6+ months may qualify without the course.
